blocks.text: The reality of scaling research operations

When you ask what does ux research look like in a scaling organization, you are really asking how to handle the pressure. Research is not a manufacturing line. Every study has different variables. As your company grows from 200 to 1,000 employees, the volume of requests grows faster than your team size.

Operational bottlenecks are the main cause of failure. Participant recruitment is the most common pain point. Without a central system, you spend hours on manual scheduling. Knowledge fragmentation is another issue. If findings are not in a shared repository, they disappear. This leads to redundant studies that confuse your stakeholders.

To keep up, you might let designers or product managers run their own tests. This is called democratization. Without guardrails, this leads to biased data. You must provide templates and training. If you do not, you risk shallow research that misleads product decisions.

faq.question: What is the biggest challenge in scaling research?
faq.answer: The biggest challenge is balancing high demand for tactical research with the need for strategic, deep-focus work while managing administrative overhead.

faq.question: How can I stop burnout as a researcher?
faq.answer: Focus on infrastructure over headcount. Use templates for common tasks and implement a research repository to reduce the time spent on repetitive synthesis.

costs.text: Important insights are lost in Slack or old documents, leading to redundant research.

costs.title: Burnout
costs.text: Constant tactical requests leave no time for strategic, high-impact research work.

causes.title: Lack of central repository
causes.text: No single source of truth means research is ephemeral and difficult to search.

causes.title: Manual recruitment
causes.text: Scheduling participants manually takes hours of back and forth communication.

causes.title: Unstructured democratization
causes.text: Allowing others to run research without training leads to poor data quality.

fixes.title: Build a repository
fixes.text: Store all findings in one place with consistent tags so you can search them later.

fixes.title: Standardize templates
fixes.text: Create study scripts and guides that others can use safely to run their own tests.

fixes.title: Set governance
fixes.text: Define who can recruit participants and where data must be stored to ensure compliance.
